notes: Consumer default is llama.cpp. Vulkan is what we run for the 35B daily driver.

First-party 35B (one R9700, llama.cpp, f16 KV). Measured on our rig, 2026-10: UD-Q5_K_XL 102.39 tok/s short / 90.52 at 32K / 66.43 at 128K / 44.4 at 256K; Q5_K_M 109.73 tok/s (24.68 GB VRAM); Q4_K_M 117.69 tok/s decode, 1902.1 tok/s prefill at 32K.
Q3 is listed as an estimate or community result unless measured. Q1/Q2 and IQ1/IQ2 stay off, including draft/MTP.
curl /v1 before you debug a harness. Do not let a desktop app download a CUDA llama.cpp on a Radeon.

engines.name: llama.cpp
engines.short: Consumer default — GGUF, Vulkan or HIP, one user
engines.well: First Qwen, debugging, a loopback /v1 for a harness, tight control of context and KV type.
engines.badly: Many concurrent clients, continuous batching, “just pip install.”
engines.run:
# not recorded: exact daily-driver command line / measured VRAM from the rig owner.
./build-vk/bin/llama-cli \
  -m ~/models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q5_K_XL.gguf \
  -ngl 99 \
  -c 262144 \
  --cache-type-k f16 \
  --cache-type-v f16 \
  -p "Say hello from a Radeon AI PRO R9700." \
  -n 64
# Server (harnesses curl this first):
./build-vk/bin/llama-server -m ~/models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q5_K_XL.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

engines.name: ExLlama / TabbyAPI
engines.short: EXL3/EXL2 server — ROCm is a side path
engines.well: EXL3/EXL2 on NVIDIA. Fast local OpenAI API if the kernels exist for your GPU.
engines.badly: A Radeon-first daily driver. Consumer RDNA FlashAttention/paged-attention is not first-class in their own issues.
engines.when: You know you need ExLlama and will build against a ROCm PyTorch that lists gfx1201 — then tell the forum what happened.
engines.run: # TabbyAPI start scripts are in their repo. No R9700 command line here.

engines.name: KTransformers / ik_llama.cpp
engines.short: CPU-heavy MoE forks — AMD is not the maintained path
engines.well: Huge MoE on a lot of RAM + NVIDIA (ik) or a 7900 XTX beta (KT).
engines.badly: gfx1201 daily driver; expecting their IQ1–IQ3 tricks (banned on this site).
engines.when: Almost never. Use llama.cpp (or Strata for Flash).
engines.run:
# python ktransformers/local_chat.py ...  (their DeepSeek example)
# We have no R9700 command line. Not documented for gfx1201.

engines.name: Lemonade Server
engines.short: AMD llama.cpp wrapper — Vulkan or ROCm on :13305
engines.well: An AMD-promoted wrapper with an explicit Vulkan vs ROCm switch, if a GPU meter moves.
engines.badly: Matching this site’s compile flags or benches; silent CPU; treating /v1 like llama-server.
engines.when: You want AMD’s server and you will read the backend log.
engines.run:
lemonade status
# lemonade pull unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q5_K_XL
# lemonade load unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q5_K_XL --ctx-size 262144 --llamacpp vulkan
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:13305/api/v1/models

engines.name: LM Studio
engines.short: Desktop app — Vulkan or a bundled ROCm runtime
engines.well: A GUI on Windows or a first desktop when you refuse to compile — if a GPU meter moves.
engines.badly: Reproducing this site’s HIP/ROCm notes; silent CPU.
engines.when: Windows-only, or a desktop, and you accept “no data” for tok/s.

engines.name: MLC-LLM
engines.well: Shipping a compiled runtime to many devices; research compilation.
engines.badly: Tracking this site’s weekly GGUF; ROCm 10.1 / gfx1201 as a documented pin.
engines.when: You have a reason to compile, not chat.
engines.run: # mlc_llm chat / serve — follow current docs. No R9700 command line here.

engines.name: Ollama
engines.short: Convenience wrapper — gfx1201 is still rocky
engines.well: Convenience, if a GPU meter moves.
engines.badly: gfx1201 as the first backend; Windows ROCm; silent CPU fallback.
engines.when: You want the wrapper and you will read the backend log.
engines.run:
ollama serve
# ollama run <tag>   # only after rocm-smi / amd-smi moves
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags

engines.badly: Daily chat; long 262K context as a first script.
engines.when: You need a training loop or a wheel check, not a harness.

engines.name: Strata
engines.short: Fast-agent try on our rig — Flash Q6
engines.well: Faster Flash Q6 agent loop than llama.cpp on the same rig, once the daily driver is already proven.
engines.badly: First install; undocumented flags; being your only engine.
engines.when: Daily driver already works and you want the fast agent.
engines.run:

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1/models
